youtube.title: Why Soda Cans Have a Dome Underneath 🥤 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
The inward dome on the bottom of a soda can is there because of pressure. Carbonated drinks push outward at roughly 2-3 times atmospheric pressure, more than a typical car tyre. A flat base would bulge and make the can unstable; a dome works like an arch, spreading the force evenly, which lets manufacturers use very thin aluminium walls and save metal.

Subscribe to The Hidden Why for a new why every day.

sources: Ball Corporation / can engineering: domed base resists internal pressure of carbonated beverages (~2-3 bar), allowing thinner walls
Sizes: aluminium can walls are about 0.1 mm thick
